title: Pocketwire Personal Account Billing Rules: Trials, Upgrade Charges, Waivers and Annual Refunds
content:
### Retired clause

The earlier Pocketwire Personal Account clause under which the plan fee was charged on each plan renewal date as a plan fee entry naming the month or year it covers — the monthly plan fee on monthly billing and the annual plan fee on annual billing — with the renewal date then moving forward one calendar month or one calendar year, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist, is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis for the renewal plan fee of the Pocketwire Personal Account. The clauses below remain in force.

### Free trial

A customer subscribing to a paid plan for the first time gets the plan's free-trial days counted from the plan started date, and the first plan fee is charged on the day after the trial ends; a customer who has subscribed to any paid plan before gets no trial.

### Upgrades

On an upgrade between two paid plans on monthly billing, the customer is charged, on the change date, the difference between the two monthly plan fees prorated by the days remaining in the current billing period, and the renewal date does not move. The proration is over the actual number of days in the current billing period. An upgrade from a free plan without a trial charges the new plan's full fee on the change date and sets the renewal date one billing cycle later.

### Waiver for restricted accounts

The monthly plan fee for a billing period is waived — no fee entry is booked — when on the renewal date the account is limited or locked and has been since a limitation or lock placement moment at least the plan's restricted-fee waiver period in calendar days earlier. The recorded moment the limitation or lock was placed is the authoritative start of the current limitation or lock.

### Annual fee refund window

An annual plan fee is refunded in full as a fee refund only when the customer cancels or downgrades within the refund window: the plan change is recorded no later than the plan's annual-fee refund window in calendar days after the annual plan fee charge date. The refund window is counted in calendar days from the annual plan fee charge date, the day after the charge being day 1, and a change on the last day of the window still qualifies. The charge date is read from the system record of the annual plan fee entry being refunded.

| Hypothetical illustration, a plan with a 14-day refund window | Refunded in full? |
|---|---|
| Plan change recorded on the 14th calendar day after the charge date | Yes — the last day of the window still qualifies |
| Plan change recorded on the 15th calendar day after the charge date | No |
| Plan change recorded on the day after the charge (day 1) | Yes |

### Fees that are never refunded

Monthly plan fees and annual fees outside the window are never refunded, whether or not the plan's benefits were used; a plan fee is not charged at all on a plan whose monthly plan fee is 0.00.
